Container.Name: FIHAS-Bot
Container.Overview:
Discord bot that watches an X/Twitter account (default @F_I_H_A_S) and posts an fxtwitter.com link to a channel whenever it tweets, pinging whoever you configure.
Click the container icon and choose WebUI to open a step-by-step setup wizard — it lists your servers, channels and roles, tests the feed sources, and previews the message. Afterwards the same page becomes a dashboard where every setting can be edited in place, so you never have to re-run the wizard.
RSSHub is BUILT IN. A private feed bridge runs inside this container, so detection does not depend on public mirrors that the whole internet shares and rate-limits. Nothing extra to install. Turn it off with "Built-in RSSHub" if you would rather use your own.
Two ways to control it from Discord: /fihas slash commands, and text commands with a prefix (default "!fihas status") for servers where slash commands never appear. Text commands need MESSAGE CONTENT INTENT enabled under Bot in the Discord Developer Portal — without it the bot still runs, it just ignores the prefix.
Discord bot permissions required: View Channels, Send Messages, Embed Links, Read Message History, and Mention @everyone only if you want @everyone pings.
The setup UI is password protected. Set "Setup UI Password" below, or leave it blank and a password is generated and printed in the container log on first start.
Config persists in /config so it survives updates and restarts. The Discord token, Application ID and Server ID are mirrored there too, so if this template ever gets re-applied and blanks those fields, the bot keeps running on the saved copy instead of dropping offline. A field with a value in it always wins, so rotating a token still works exactly as you would expect.
AFTER YOU HIT APPLY, delete fihas-bot.xml from /boot/config/plugins/dockerMan/templates-user/ and keep only my-FIHAS-Bot.xml. Both files declare the same container name, and leaving this one behind is what lets an Apply or Force Update reset your settings to the defaults below.

Config.Name: Discord Bot Token
Config.Description: Bot token from the Discord Developer Portal (Bot -> Reset Token). Keep this secret.

Config.Name: Discord Application ID
Config.Description: Application ID from the Discord Developer Portal (General Information).

Config.Name: Discord Server ID
Config.Description: Your server ID. Strongly recommended: slash commands register instantly instead of taking up to an hour.

Config.Name: Setup UI Password
Config.Description: Password for the setup wizard WebUI. Leave blank to have one generated and printed in the container log on first start.

Config.Name: Text Command Prefix
Config.Description: Prefix for text commands, e.g. "!fihas status". Use this when slash commands do not show up in your server. Requires MESSAGE CONTENT INTENT to be enabled under Bot in the Discord Developer Portal.

Config.Name: Enable Text Commands
Config.Description: Set to false to ignore the prefix and use slash commands only. When false the bot does not request the Message Content intent at all.

Config.Name: Voice Playback Volume
Config.Description: Default volume for "/fihas play", 0-200, as a percentage of the clip as recorded. 100 is loud in a busy channel. Leave blank to edit it in the WebUI under Voice playback instead.

Config.Name: Built-in RSSHub
Config.Description: Runs the RSSHub bundled into this image as a private feed source (about 150MB of RAM). Set to false to rely on public mirrors or your own RSSHub instead.

Config.Name: X Handle
Config.Description: Account to watch, without the @.

Config.Name: Discord Channel ID
Config.Description: Optional. Channel to post in. You can also set this later with /fihas channel set.

Config.Name: Ping Role IDs
Config.Description: Optional. Comma-separated role IDs to ping on a new post. Also settable with /fihas ping add.

Config.Name: Poll Interval (seconds)
Config.Description: How often to check for new posts. Minimum 30.

Config.Name: RSS Feed URLs
Config.Description: Optional. Comma-separated RSS feeds tried in order. Leave blank to use the built-in RSSHub plus public mirrors as fallbacks. Setting this replaces that list entirely.

Config.Name: RSS Fetch Timeout (seconds)
Config.Description: Optional. How long a feed has to answer before the bot moves on to the next one, 5-120. Leave blank to manage it in the WebUI under RSS & sources; a value here is applied whenever you change it in this template.

Config.Name: RSS Items Per Fetch
Config.Description: Optional. How many of the newest items to read from each feed, 1-100. Leave blank to manage it in the WebUI under RSS & sources.

Config.Name: RSS User Agent
Config.Description: Optional. Sent when fetching feeds; some mirrors block unfamiliar clients. Leave blank for the bot's own user agent, or edit it in the WebUI under RSS & sources.

Config.Name: RSSHub X Auth Token
Config.Description: Optional. The auth_token cookie from a logged-in X session, used by the built-in RSSHub to read timelines. Without one, RSSHub answers 503 for every X request. You can also paste it into the WebUI under RSS & sources, which restarts RSSHub with it straight away and takes precedence over this field — handy because X expires these often. See https://docs.rsshub.app/deploy/config#x-twitter. Any other RSSHub variable can be added here as an extra variable too.

Config.Name: X API Bearer Token
Config.Description: Optional. Only works on a paid X API plan (Basic or higher); the free tier cannot read timelines. When set, it is tried before RSS.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Persistent config and the list of already-posted tweet IDs.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Setup wizard and dashboard. Also serves an unauthenticated /healthz endpoint used for the container health check.

Config.Name: RSSHub Port
Config.Description: Optional. The built-in RSSHub. The bot reaches it inside the container without this, so only map it if you want to use the feed bridge from elsewhere on your network. Remove this port if 1200 is already taken.

Config.Name: Timezone
Config.Description: Container timezone, e.g. Europe/London.
